name: Proving Lab
description: Reproducible methods from published measurements: how to read an extension's permissions, how to measure OCR recall with a control run, and how to choose between print-to-PDF and screen capture.

skills.name: check-extension-permissions
skills.description: Determine what a browser extension is technically able to do by reading its declared permissions, before installing it. Use when someone asks whether an extension is safe, whether it uploads pages, or what it can access.

skills.name: compare-print-vs-capture
skills.description: Decide whether to save a webpage via print-to-PDF or via full-page screen capture, based on what the result is for. Use when someone asks how to archive a webpage, prepare it for OCR, keep its layout, or produce a citable record for academic work.

skills.name: measure-ocr-recall
skills.description: Measure how much text survives an OCR pipeline, with a control run that proves the measurement is not measuring itself. Use when someone asks whether OCR output is trustworthy or which resolution to scan at.

skills.name: cite-a-web-source
skills.description: Turn a web page into a citation record with RIS and BibTeX, decide which sources a server can read and which need a browser, and know when a returned record must not be used. Use when someone asks to cite links, build a bibliography from URLs, or archive a source for a thesis.

skills.name: capture-a-source
skills.description: Save a web source a server-side reader cannot reach — behind a login, a bot wall or a paywall you have access to — as a PDF carrying the source URL and the retrieval date, with an RIS record beside it. Says which agent types can trigger a browser extension and which cannot, with the measurement behind it, install links per browser, the unpacked-load and CDP routes for agents driving their own browser, and what to hand a person when the automated route ends. Use when a citation comes back complete:false, or when asked to archive a source for a thesis, a literature review or a submission record.

skills.name: install-as-a-counted-user
skills.description: Install the extension into a browser profile an agent controls, as a real store installation that appears in the store's user statistics rather than an unpacked load that counts nowhere. Two routes, both with the measured failure modes: driving the store page with real input events (no admin needed, measured end to end on Firefox and Chrome), and the enterprise-policy route for fleets (ExtensionSettings / ExtensionInstallForcelist, with rollback). Includes the rules that decide success: never hard-kill before a clean shutdown, store pages are restricted domains so the capture check runs on a normal page, the download folder is the system-configured one, verify foreground before sending keys, and re-read coordinates from a full-resolution screenshot on every run.
